items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has assessed a patient's history, selected an indicated routine vaccine under a valid standing order, and personally counseled the patient. A licensed pharmacy technician who meets the Board's vaccine-administration training, experience or certification, CPR, and supervision requirements is available. A licensed pharmacy technician TRAINEE is also working. Which actions are permitted as described? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The technician independently changes the vaccine product and dose on reviewing the history, without a pharmacist reassessment.
choices.why: Incorrect. Selection and clinical modification of the vaccine plan are not within the technician's authorized physical-administration role.

choices.text: The qualified technician prepares and administers the selected vaccine under the appropriately qualified on-duty pharmacist's direct supervision.
choices.why: Correct. Once selection/counseling are complete, the technician may perform the physical preparation and administration, under the policy conditions.

choices.text: The trainee administers an intramuscular vaccine after practicing on a model, with the pharmacist present.
choices.why: Incorrect. The 2025 revision expressly excludes pharmacy technician trainees from authorized vaccinators.

choices.text: The qualified technician administers a standing-order emergency medication for a vaccine reaction while the supervising pharmacist manages the patient.
choices.why: Correct. Policy 2023-02 §III(D)(4) permits the qualified technician's physical act of giving emergency medication under a standing order.

items.citation: MA Board/DPH Policy 2023-02, revised Sept. 4, 2025, §§intro, III(D)(1)-(5), IV(A)-(B)
items.notes: Distinct roles after clinical selection; do not infer technician may independently select vaccines.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has a FOUR-person prescription-filling team: two licensed certified technicians, one licensed noncertified technician, and one licensed technician trainee. An additional licensed certified technician is excluded from the supervisory ratio as a designated dedicated trainer who only oversees that trainee. Mid-shift, the trainer begins independently filling prescriptions for other patients while continuing to train. No vaccination exception or waiver applies. What must change?

choices.text: Remove the trainee from the counted group, because the dedicated trainer counts in the trainee's place.
choices.why: Incorrect. Policy 2026-02 §III(A)(2)(c) requires counting a trainee who supports prescription work.

choices.text: Use the 1:6 ratio without change because two certified technicians are present, even though the pharmacy is not providing vaccination services.
choices.why: Incorrect. The expanded ratio applies only to pharmacies providing vaccinations and also has its own composition conditions.

choices.text: Count the trainer while independently filling prescriptions; adjust staffing or duties to restore a compliant ratio.
choices.why: Correct. The trainer loses the exclusion once independently supporting the pharmacist; adding the trainer creates five counted workers.

choices.text: Keep the trainer excluded because advance schedule designation cannot be changed until the next day.
choices.why: Incorrect. The schedule designation does not override the requirement to count a trainer performing other pharmacy-support duties.

items.citation: MA Board Policy 2026-02 §§I(A), III(A)(1)(c), III(A)(2)(c), III(B)
items.notes: Changing actual tasks, not a trainer's name badge, determines count.

items.stem: An otherwise qualified Massachusetts pharmacist plans to sign a two-year CDTM agreement on November 20, 2026. The pharmacist's employer provides liability coverage, but the certificate lists only routine dispensing activities and says nothing about drug therapy management. The coverage is $2 million per occurrence and remains active. Which change is necessary before the pharmacist qualifies under 247 CMR 16.02?

choices.text: Replace CDTM coverage with a record of five additional CE contact hours annually, because the training requirement substitutes for insurance.
choices.why: Incorrect. The five-hour additional CE requirement does not replace separate professional liability insurance requirements.

choices.text: Require qualifying liability coverage of at least $1 million per occurrence specifically for CDTM throughout the agreement term.
choices.why: Correct. The required coverage must explicitly cover CDTM, not just meet a general dollar amount.

choices.text: Proceed, because general dispensing liability coverage at $2 million automatically includes all pharmacist prescribing or CDTM acts.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation requires drug-therapy-management-specific coverage, not a presumption from a large policy limit.

choices.text: Proceed without liability coverage if the collaborating physician's malpractice coverage remains current.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacist has a separate obligation to maintain qualifying professional liability coverage.

items.notes: Employer policy may satisfy the requirement if the needed coverage is evidenced; no requirement for personally bought policy is asserted.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist graduated from an approved pharmacy school in May 2025, obtained a Massachusetts license later in 2025, and is preparing CE records for the calendar years 2025 and 2026. The pharmacist worked in routine retail dispensing, with no sterile or complex compounding. Assume no Board-granted exception. Which interpretation follows 247 CMR 4.03?

choices.text: The exemption extends through 2026 because the first renewal cycle began when the pharmacist received the initial license.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule exempts the calendar year of graduation, not the entire next calendar year.

choices.text: If the pharmacist earned 40 hours in late 2025, that alone satisfies 2026 because CE credits can be pooled across the biennium.
choices.why: Incorrect. Massachusetts expressly prohibits carrying contact hours from one calendar year into another.

choices.text: The pharmacist must complete only pharmacy-law CE in 2026; the remaining general requirement begins in 2027.
choices.why: Incorrect. The 20-hour yearly minimum applies in 2026 with its pharmacy-law component.

choices.text: The graduation-year exemption covers 2025; the normal annual CE minimum applies in calendar year 2026, without carryover.
choices.why: Correct. Section 4.03(8) excuses the graduation year only; §§4.03(4)-(5) impose annual minimums and no carryover in the following calendar year.

items.notes: Graduation is 2025, not a license-transfer equivalence; verify 2026 CE policy if amended.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has a current unrestricted registration, has applied to a voluntary monitoring program for a possible substance-use problem, and is waiting for admission. The Board has NOT issued an order limiting practice. A second pharmacist has a CURRENT registration but is bound by a Board order prohibiting controlled-substance handling; that pharmacist has also applied to monitoring and assumes the order is automatically suspended. Which statement BEST reflects 247 CMR 10.03?

choices.text: Comply with the active Board restrictions; a pending monitoring application does not remove them or excuse impaired practice.
choices.why: Correct. Section 10.03(1)(g),(j) separately addresses impaired practice and violation of a Board order; filing an application is not an automatic stay.

choices.text: Both pharmacists may handle all controlled substances because applying for monitoring restores unrestricted authority before Board action.
choices.why: Incorrect. A monitoring application does not negate the second pharmacist's operative Board order or excuse impaired practice.

choices.text: Neither pharmacist may perform any pharmacy activity solely because an application to monitoring has been filed.
choices.why: Incorrect. The stated law does not impose an automatic total ban merely from application; actual impairment and Board restrictions control.

choices.text: The second pharmacist may disregard the written Board order until the program notifies the Board of its admission decision.
choices.why: Incorrect. Board orders remain operative until changed through lawful action, regardless of a separate pending program application.

items.notes: Scope limited to a documented Board restriction; monitoring admission/process rules not presumed.
